message.content:
Below is a concise summary of your key rights and protections as a residential tenant in Texas (as of 2026). These are drawn from Texas Property Code, local ordinances, and court precedent. For detailed advice tailored to your situation, consider consulting a qualified attorney or a local tenant‑rights organization. | Area | Your Rights | Practical Tips | |------|-------------|----------------| | **Security Deposit** | • Landlord may charge up to one month’s rent for a furnished unit, two months for an unfurnished unit.
• Must be returned within 30 days after you move out, minus lawful deductions. | • Keep a written inventory at move‑in and move‑out.
• Get a receipt for the deposit. | | **Habitability & Repairs** | • Landlord must keep premises safe, sanitary, and fit for habitation (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical).
• You can withhold rent if major repairs are not made within a reasonable time. | • Document problems (photos, written notices).
• Send a certified letter requesting repair; keep copies. | | **Notice Requirements** | • For non‑payment of rent: 3‑day notice to pay or vacate.
• For lease termination: 30‑day notice for month‑to‑month tenancy; 60‑days for longer leases.
• For entry: 24‑hour notice unless emergency. | • Use a written notice (email or certified mail) and keep proof. | | **Eviction Process** | • Landlord must file a complaint in district court.
• Court will issue a summons and order a hearing.
• If you’re found liable, you have 10 days to pay or contest. | • Attend all hearings; bring evidence (rent receipts, repair requests). | | **Discrimination** | • Protected under federal Fair Housing Act and Texas Civil Rights Act: race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, source of income, etc. | • Report violations to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) or Texas Commission on Human Rights. | | **Lease Terms** | • Lease cannot contain illegal clauses (e.g., waiving your right to sue).
• You can negotiate terms before signing. | • Read the lease carefully; ask questions about ambiguous language. | | **Right to Quiet Enjoyment** | • Landlord must respect your privacy and not interfere with your use of the property. | • Notify landlord of any disturbances; document incidents. | | **Subletting / Assignment** | • Generally allowed unless lease prohibits it; landlord cannot unreasonably deny sublease. | • Obtain written permission; keep records of subtenant agreements. | | **Utilities & Services** | • Landlord must maintain essential services (water, heat, electricity). | • Verify who pays utilities; keep utility bills as proof. | | **Rent Increases** | • No statutory limit on increases, but must comply with lease terms and give proper notice. | • Review lease for escalation clauses; check local ordinances for caps. | | **Legal Remedies** | • Can sue for unpaid rent, damages, or unlawful eviction.
• Can seek a protective order if threatened or harassed. | • Preserve all correspondence, receipts, and photos. | ### Quick Checklist Before Moving In 1. **Get a Written Lease** – Ensure it includes rent amount, due date, security deposit, maintenance responsibilities, and notice periods. 2. **Document Condition** – Take dated photos/video of each room, appliances, and common areas. 3. **Ask About Utilities** – Clarify which utilities you’ll pay and how they’re metered. 4. **Know Local Ordinances** – Some cities (e.g., Austin, Dallas) have additional tenant protections beyond state law. ### Resources - **Texas Attorney General – Consumer Protection Division** – Provides consumer guides on rental housing. - **Texas Commission on Human Rights** – Handles discrimination complaints. - **Local Tenant‑Rights Groups** – e.g., “Austin Tenants Union,” “Dallas Housing Advocacy.” - **U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD)** – Offers nationwide fair‑housing resources. --- If you need a sample lease or a more detailed contract for a specific scenario (e.g., month‑to‑month agreement, sublease), let me know and I can generate a template using the `generate_contract` tool.
